paragraphs: We are a leading innovator in surgical treatments and therapies for atrial fibrillation (Afib or AF), left atrial appendage (LAA) management and post-operative pain management. Afib is an irregular heartbeat, or arrhythmia, which affects over 59 million people worldwide and is a growing epidemic. It is the most common cardiac arrhythmia encountered in clinical practice and results in high utilization of healthcare services and significant cost burden. Patients often progress from being in Afib intermittently (paroxysmal) to being in Afib continuously (non-paroxysmal). The continuous Afib patient population includes early persistent Afib, which lasts seven days to six months, persistent Afib, which lasts six months to one year, and long-standing persistent Afib, which lasts longer than one year. It is estimated that over four million people in the United States currently suffer from long-standing persistent Afib. Afib often occurs in conjunction with other cardiovascular diseases, including hypertension, congestive heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction, coronary artery disease and valvular disease.

Our cardiac ablation and left atrial appendage management (LAAM) products are used by physicians during open-heart and minimally invasive surgical procedures. In open-heart procedures, the patient is undergoing heart surgery for other conditions, such as a mitral or aortic valve repair or a coronary artery bypass, and our products are used by physicians in conjunction with ("concomitant" to) such a procedure. Minimally invasive procedures are performed on a standalone basis, and often include multi-disciplinary or "hybrid" approaches, combining surgical procedures using our ablation and LAAM products with catheter ablation performed by an electrophysiologist.

Our pain management solutions are used by physicians to freeze nerves during cardiac, thoracic or amputation surgical procedures. Recovery from these surgeries can be complicated and painful. Many surgeons use multiple pain management strategies that include oral delivery of opioid and non-opioid pain medications. Our cryoICE cryoSPHERE® and cryoXT™ probes for pain management (known as Cryo Nerve Block) provide temporary relief of post-operative pain, allowing the patient's body to heal after surgery while the nerves regenerate and sensation is regained.

We sell our products to medical centers through our direct sales force in the United States, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, the Benelux region, Australia and Canada. We also sell our products through distributors who in turn sell our products to medical centers in other international markets. Our business is primarily transacted in U.S. Dollars; direct sales transactions outside the United States are primarily transacted in Euros, British Pounds, Australian Dollars or Canadian Dollars.

Afib is the most commonly diagnosed sustained cardiac arrhythmia, with over one million diagnoses annually in the United States alone. Afib is also an under-diagnosed condition due in large part to the fact that patients with Afib often have mild or no symptoms, and their Afib is diagnosed when they seek treatment for an associated condition, such as a structural heart disease or stroke. Symptoms of Afib may include heart palpitations, dizziness, fatigue and shortness of breath, and these symptoms may be debilitating and life threatening in some cases. When a patient is in Afib, abnormal electrical impulses cause the atria, or upper chambers of the heart, to fibrillate, or beat rapidly, irregularly and in an uncoordinated fashion. As a result, blood in the atria may be in stasis, increasing the risk that a blood clot will form and cause a stroke or other serious complications. In patients with Afib, a significant percentage of those clots can form inside of the LAA. We believe that increasing awareness of Afib and improved diagnostic screening will result in an increased number of patients diagnosed with Afib over time. Also, since the prevalence of Afib increases with age, there will likely be an increase in the number of diagnosed Afib patients globally as the world population ages.

Afib is a condition that doctors often find difficult to treat and, historically, there has been no widely accepted long-term cure for Afib. This difficulty is exacerbated with more serious forms of Afib, or persistent and long-standing persistent Afib. Over the past two decades, technological advancements have made surgical ablation more effective, repeatable and available to cardiac surgeons and electrophysiologists around the world. Societal guidelines from the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS), Heart Rhythm Society (HRS) and American Association of Thoracic Surgery (AATS) have Class I recommendations for concomitant surgical ablation, meaning that it is a "recommended" treatment for patients who have structural heart disease and Afib. Guidelines for the treatment of more serious forms of Afib for patients without structural heart disease have also been introduced in the past several years. In 2024, the European Society of Cardiology (ESC) released Guidelines for Management of Atrial Fibrillation developed in collaboration with the European Association

of Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS), in which they upgraded LAAM to the highest Class 1 recommendation. During 2023, the American College of Cardiology (ACC), American Heart Association (AHA), American College of Clinical Pharmacy (ACCP) and HRS released Guidelines for Diagnosis and Management of Atrial Fibrillation, and upgraded LAAM to the highest recommendation of Class 1 and now include Hybrid AF™ Therapy as a Class 2 recommendation. These societal guidelines are reflective of the scientific evidence suggesting that surgical and hybrid ablation is safe and effective for patients who have Afib. Of the patients undergoing open-heart surgery globally on an annual basis, we estimate that over 500,000 are potential candidates for surgical ablation using our products, as they have pre-operative Afib. Today, we estimate that less than 15% of those candidates are being treated with surgical ablation. Therefore, we believe that the market for our ablation products represents a significant growth opportunity.

In addition, Afib is thought to be responsible for approximately 15% to 20% of the estimated 800,000 strokes that occur annually in the United States. According to the American Heart Association, the risk of stroke is five times higher in people with Afib. Studies have also suggested that 90% of clots that cause strokes in patients who have Afib originate from within the LAA. In 2021, a large independent international randomized trial, Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion Study (LAAOS) III, demonstrated a significant reduction in strokes when the LAA was managed during cardiac surgery. Afib accounts for billions of dollars in hospitalization-related and office visit costs in the United States each year. Indirect costs, such as the management of Afib-related strokes, are also believed to be significant. Due to the risk of stroke and the significant cost burden on the healthcare system, more and more surgeons are routinely addressing the LAA, both in patients who have Afib and in those who do not have Afib but may be at increased risk of developing the disease in the future. We believe that our AtriClip system is safer, more effective and easier to use than other products and techniques for excluding the LAA during cardiac surgery. Additionally, our Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion for Prophylactic Stroke Reduction (LeAAPS) IDE clinical trial is evaluating the safety and effectiveness of our AtriClip system in reducing stroke in cardiac surgery patients without a pre-existing Afib diagnosis. Our Box Lesion and Left Atrial Appendage EXclusion Procedure for the Prevention of New Onset of Atrial Fibrillation (BoxX-NoAF) IDE trial evaluates the impact of concomitant ablation using the EnCompass clamp and the AtriClip system in non-AF patients for the reduction of post-operative Afib (POAF) and clinical AF. Therefore, we believe that the market for our AtriClip system represents a significant growth opportunity.

Many Afib patients without other underlying structural heart disease, especially those with more advanced forms of Afib, are symptomatic and experience conditions such as palpitations, breathlessness and drowsiness. These patients tend to be motivated to seek treatment to alleviate their symptoms. Patients who are symptomatic are often treated by an electrophysiologist using catheter ablation. Catheter ablation is considered a percutaneous procedure that does not require the opening of the chest; rather, catheters are inserted through a small puncture in the groin. In addition to catheter ablation, there are other treatment options for patients with Afib, including pharmacological therapy (anti-arrhythmic drugs) and implantable pacemakers. It is estimated that approximately 500,000 Afib patients are treated by catheter ablation every year in the United States, a number that is expected to see significant continued growth. While the majority of paroxysmal Afib patients treated by catheter ablation tend to experience freedom from Afib, less than a third of long-standing persistent patients treated by catheter ablation are cured of their Afib at one year, and it declines even more thereafter. Randomized, prospective, multi-center data from the CONVERGE™ IDE clinical trial, along with a number of other recent real-world studies performed by physician investigators, show that these long-standing persistent Afib patients can experience more than double the success rate by adding an ablation on the outside surface of the heart using our EPi-Sense® ablation system. Thus, we believe the EPi-Sense ablation system used as a minimally invasive or Hybrid AF therapy also represents a growth opportunity for the Company.

Beyond the Afib treatment opportunity, it is estimated that up to 50% of patients who undergo cardiac surgery who do not have diagnosed pre-operative Afib eventually develop POAF. Patients with POAF tend to have worse acute and long-term clinical outcomes, including the risk of developing long-term clinical Afib. Additionally, various studies have associated POAF with higher healthcare cost related burdens. Currently, there are no FDA approved therapies to prevent the onset of POAF in cardiac surgery patients. In October, we enrolled the first patient in the BoxX-NoAF IDE trial, which is intended to demonstrate that ablation and left atrial appendage exclusion during cardiac surgery is safe and effective for reducing POAF and long-term clinical Afib in patients without a documented pre-operative history of Afib. If the trial is successful, we believe this significantly expands our addressable market for concomitant ablation and LAAM to be inclusive of non-Afib patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

Thoracic surgery involving an incision through the ribcage, typically referred to as thoracotomy access, and cardiothoracic surgery can often result in significant post-operative pain and longer hospital recovery times as patients refrain from mobilizing their chest near the incision site. It is estimated that each year approximately 150,0000 thoracic procedures and approximately 250,000 cardiothoracic procedures are performed in the United States. Hospital recovery times can vary from two to fifteen days depending on the procedure, operative complications associated with the

procedure, pain management protocol and other factors. Most surgeons will employ a multi-modal pain management protocol that includes various pain management techniques, including techniques such as epidural delivery of medication directly around the spinal cord, intravenous or oral delivery of opioid and non-opioid pain medications, or other strategies. More focused, local techniques include syringe injections between vertebrates and Cryo Nerve Block which uses cryogenic energy to ablate peripheral nerves, temporarily stopping the transmission of pain signals coming from the chest wall during surgery. The nerve "scaffolds" remain intact, allowing axons to regenerate and restore nerve function over time. Cryo Nerve Block can be delivered using our cryoICE cryoSPHERE probes, which are specifically designed for Cryo Nerve Block therapy. Depending on the degree of invasiveness, physicians and their nursing staff will take advantage of multiple ways of managing pain for their patients. In recent years, prescription narcotics, or opioids, have come under heavy scrutiny due to their potential for long-term dependency, overdose and possible death. Both federal and local governments in the United States have proposed and implemented new regulations to curb the opioid overdose epidemic. It is also estimated that one in seven thoracic surgery patients develops an unhealthy post-procedural addiction to prescription narcotics, making alternative, non-opioid pain management modalities, such as Cryo Nerve Block, an increasingly important part of how physicians manage post-operative pain. We believe the market for our pain management ablation products represents a significant growth opportunity. In September 2025, we announced the launch of the cryoXT™ device, an innovative cryoablation technology used to help manage post-operative pain following amputation procedures. Each year, over 180,000 amputations occur in the U.S., with approximately 60% of patients experiencing residual limb pain and up to 85% reporting phantom limb pain. With the introduction of the cryoXT device, physicians now have access to a next-generation tool that brings this long-lasting approach to post-amputation pain management. Applications for Cryo Nerve Block outside of cardiac, thoracic, and amputation surgery are being studied and represent future possible growth opportunities

We believe that we are currently the market leader in the surgical treatment of Afib and LAAM, and pioneers of the application of Cryo Nerve Block in cardiac, thoracic and amputation surgical procedures. We anticipate that substantially all our revenue for the foreseeable future will relate to products we currently sell or are in the process of developing. Our products enable surgeons to perform ablation and LAAM procedures with faster, less invasive and less technically challenging approaches and clinically proven results. We have completed, and continue to invest in, clinical studies for the use of our ablation and LAAM products to treat Afib, reduce post-operative Afib, and prevent strokes. Leading surgeons and electrophysiologists, including those who serve or who have served as consultants to us, have published results of preclinical and clinical studies utilizing our devices. The results of these studies have assessed efficacy, ease of use and safety endpoints.

Products for cardiac tissue ablation include those that create scar tissue using radio frequency (RF) energy or cryogenic (cryo) modalities. Our ablation products are part of platforms, each consisting of disposable hand pieces which connect to either a RF generator or a cryo generator. We generally place this capital equipment with our direct customers and sell to our distributors.

headings: Commercial Execution and Product Performance Risks
If our products do not achieve widespread market acceptance in the United States, our operating results will be harmed, and we may not achieve or sustain profitability.
Competition from existing and new products and procedures may decrease our market share and may cause our revenue to decline, and could adversely affect our operating results.

Any clinical data that is generated regarding our products may not be positive, and our current and planned clinical trials may not satisfy the requirements of the FDA or other regulatory authorities.
A prolonged downturn in macroeconomic conditions may materially and adversely affect our business.

Healthcare costs have risen significantly over the past decade. There have been and may continue to be proposals by legislators, regulators and third-party payors to contain or reduce healthcare costs.
Adverse changes in governmental and third-party payors' policies toward coverage and reimbursement for surgical procedures would harm our ability to promote and sell our products.
We rely upon single and limited source third-party suppliers and third-party service providers, making us vulnerable to supply problems and price fluctuations which could harm our business.
Our manufacturing operations are highly centralized, and disruption at our manufacturing facilities could increase our expenses and decrease our revenue.
If we fail to properly manage our anticipated growth, our business could suffer.
Disruptions of critical information systems or material breaches in the security of our systems could harm our business, customer relations and financial condition.
Our insurance may not cover our indemnification obligations and other liabilities associated with our operations.

We spend considerable time and money complying with federal, state and foreign regulations in addition to FDA regulations, and, if we do not fully comply with such regulations, we could face substantial penalties.

If we fail to comply with the extensive FDA regulations relating to our business, we may be subject to fines, injunctions and penalties, and our ability to commercially distribute and promote our products may be hurt.
The use of products we sell may result in injuries or other adverse events that lead to product liability suits, which could be costly to our business or our customers' businesses.

The following is a summary of the principal risks that could adversely affect our business, operations, financial results and stock price.
•Failure to achieve widespread market acceptance domestically may harm operating results.
•Competition from existing and new products and procedures may decrease our market share.

•Clinical data may be negative, or our trials may not satisfy requirements of regulatory authorities, slowing or reversing the rate of adoption or reducing use of our products by the medical community.
•Reliance on independent distributors to sell our products in some international markets could adversely impact our sales.

We sell our products to medical centers through our direct sales force in the United States, Germany, France, the United Kingdom, the Benelux region, Australia and Canada. In 2025, we realized global revenue growth resulting from our strategic initiatives of product innovation, clinical science and physician education and training to expand awareness and adoption. Our worldwide revenues for the year ended December 31, 2025 of $534,528 increased by 14.9% over the prior year, driven by expanding adoption of our pain management, open ablation and appendage management product lines. Our recent product launches, including our cryoSPHERE MAX probe, AtriClip FLEX-Mini device and EnCompass clamp meaningfully contributed to our growth in 2025. There are limited competitors in our key markets; however, new entrants are developing and marketing competing products, procedures, and/or clinical solutions that may cause variability in our results.
Highlights of the strategic and operational advancements in 2025 include:

Appendage management. During the first quarter of 2025, FDA granted 510(k) clearance for the AtriClip® PRO-Mini™ LAA Exclusion System. The device is built on the existing AtriClip platform, preloaded with the smallest surgical LAA management implant available in the market. The size reduction provides surgeons with enhanced visualization for precise, secure exclusion of the LAA during minimally invasive procedures. The AtriClip PRO-Mini device was launched in the United States during the second half of 2025.

Pain management. During the second quarter of 2025, FDA granted 510(k) clearance for the cryoICE® cryoXT™ probe, a cryoablation device designed specifically for Cryo Nerve Block therapy to alleviate pain in amputation patients. This device temporarily stops pain by freezing target peripheral nerves, blocking the conduction pathway at the site of amputation. During the third quarter of 2025, this device was launched in the United States.

Dual energy platform. During the fourth quarter of 2025, we executed successful first-in-human treatments using our novel dual energy platform that integrates Pulsed Field Ablation (PFA) with Advanced Radiofrequency Ablation (Advanced RFA). The new platform delivers the benefits of both technologies, combining the proven safety and

effectiveness of radiofrequency (RF) ablation with the efficiency of PFA. The Advanced RFA and PFA technologies are not yet approved for use in any market. We expect to initiate a clinical trial in the coming year, marking a key milestone in our product development pipeline.

CLINICAL SCIENCE. We invest in studies to expand labeling claims, support various indications for our products and publish clinical data for therapies and procedures involving our products. During 2025, we supported the publication of 13 articles and 15 congress abstracts featuring clinical studies with our products.

LeAAPS. The Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion for Prophylactic Stroke Reduction (LeAAPS) IDE clinical trial is designed to evaluate the effectiveness of prophylactic LAA exclusion using the AtriClip LAA Exclusion System for the prevention of ischemic stroke or systemic arterial embolism in cardiac surgery patients without pre-operative AF diagnosis who are at risk for these events. This prospective, multicenter, randomized trial evaluates safety at 30 days post-procedure to demonstrate no increased risk with LAA exclusion during cardiac surgery, and efficacy over a minimum follow-up of five years post procedure. In July 2025, we completed trial enrollment of 6,573 patients across 139 centers globally. Patient follow-up remains ongoing.

BoxX-NoAF. The Box Lesion and Left Atrial Appendage EXclusion Procedure for the Prevention of New Onset of Atrial Fibrillation (BoxX-NoAF) IDE trial evaluates the impact of concomitant ablation using the EnCompass clamp and LAA exclusion with the AtriClip system in non-AF patients for the reduction of post-operative AF (POAF) and Clinical AF. This prospective, multi-center, multi-national randomized trial evaluates safety at 30 days post-procedure for POAF and secondary effectiveness for Clinical AF through three years. The trial provides enrollment of up to 960 subjects at up to 75 sites globally. FDA approved the trial protocol during the fourth quarter of 2024 and during October 2025, we completed the first patient enrollment. Site initiation and enrollment is ongoing.

paragraphs: 本公司為心臟電生理治療與療法領域的領導創新者，專注於心房顫動（Afib 或 AF）、左心耳管理（LAA）及術後疼痛管理。心房顫動是一種不規則心跳，或稱心律不整，影響全球超過 59 百萬人，且為日益嚴重的流行病。心房顫動是臨牀上最常見的心臟心律不整，導致高比例的醫療服務使用與顯著的醫療成本負擔。患者常從偶發性心房顫動（paroxysmal）進展為持續性心房顫動（non-paroxysmal）。持續性心房顫動患者羣包括早期持續性心房顫動，持續時間為七日至六個月，持續性心房顫動，持續時間為六個月至一年，以及長期持續性心房顫動，持續時間超過一年。估計美國目前有超過四百萬人患有長期持續性心房顫動。心房顫動常與其他心血管疾病同時發生，包括高血壓、心衰竭、左心室功能障礙、冠狀動脈疾病及瓣膜疾病。
本公司的心臟消融與左心耳管理（LAAM）產品由醫師在開胸手術及微創手術期間使用。在開胸手術中，患者接受其他條件的心臟手術，例如二尖瓣或主動脈瓣修補或冠狀動脈繞道手術，而本公司產品由醫師與此手術同時使用（稱為 concomitant）。微創手術則為獨立進行，常包含多學科或「混合」方式，結合使用本公司消融與 LAAM 產品的手術與電生理學家執行的導管消融手術。
本公司疼痛管理解決方案由醫師在心臟、胸部或截肢手術期間使用，用以冷凍神經。這些手術的復原過程可能複雜且疼痛。許多外科醫生會使用多種疼痛管理策略，包括口服給予阿片類與非阿片類止痛藥物。本公司 cryoICE cryoSPHERE® 與 cryoXT™ 探針用於疼痛管理（稱為 Cryo Nerve Block），可提供術後疼痛的暫時緩解，使患者身體能於手術後恢復，同時神經再生與感覺恢復。
本公司將產品銷售給美國、德國、法國、英國、比利時-荷蘭-盧森堡地區、澳洲與加拿大等地的醫療中心，透過本公司直接銷售團隊。本公司亦透過經銷商銷售產品，經銷商再將產品銷售至其他國際市場的醫療中心。本公司業務主要以美金進行交易；直接銷售交易於美國以外地區，則主要以歐元、英鎊、澳洲幣或加拿大幣進行交易。

Afib 是最常被診斷的持續性心臟心律不整症，僅美國每年就診斷出超過 1 百萬例。Afib 也是被低估的病症，主要原因在於患有 Afib 的病患常有輕微或無症狀，而他們的 Afib 是在尋求治療相關病症（如結構性心臟病或中風）時才被診斷出來。Afib 的症狀可能包括心悸、暈眩、疲勞和呼吸急促，這些症狀在某些情況下可能導致癱瘓或危及生命。當病患處於 Afib 時，異常的電氣衝動會導致心房（心臟的上部房室）產生顫動，或快速、不規則且無協調地跳動。結果，心房內的血液可能靜止不流動，增加血塊形成並導致中風或其他嚴重併發症的風險。在患有 Afib 的病患中，有相當比例的血塊會在左心耳（LAA）內形成。我們認為，提高對 Afib 的認知以及改善診斷篩檢，將會使未來診斷出 Afib 的病患數量增加。此外，由於 Afib 的盛行率隨年齡增加而上升，因此全球人口老化將導致診斷出 Afib 的病患數量也將增加。

Afib 是醫生常認為難以治療的病症，歷史上也沒有廣為接受的長期治療方法。這種困難在更嚴重的 Afib 類型（如持續性及長期持續性 Afib）中更為顯著。過去二十年來，技術進步使手術消融更有效、可重複且可供全球心臟外科醫生和電生理學家使用。胸外科學會（STS）、心律學會（HRS）和美國胸外科學會（AATS）的社會指引已將同時進行手術消融列入一級推薦，表示這是對有結構性心臟病及 Afib 病患的「建議」治療方式。對於沒有結構性心臟病的更嚴重 Afib 類型病患的治療指引也已在過去幾年中推出。2024 年，歐洲心臟病學會（ESC）與歐洲心臟外科學會（EACTS）合作發佈了《心房顫動管理指引》，其中將 LAAM 提升為最高一級推薦。在 2023 年，美國心臟學會（ACC）、美國心臟協會（AHA）、美國臨牀藥物學會（ACCP）和 HRS 發佈了《心房顫動診斷與管理指引》，並將 LAAM 提升為最高一級推薦，並將 Hybrid AF™ 療法列入二級推薦。這些社會指引反映了科學證據，顯示手術及混合消融對患有 Afib 的病患是安全且有效的。

於心血管外科手術學會（EACTS）中，他們將LAAM升級為最高階的Class 1建議。在2023年，美國心臟病學會（ACC）、美國心臟協會（AHA）、美國臨牀藥物學會（ACCP）及HRS發布了房顫診斷與管理指南，並將LAAM升級為最高階的Class 1建議，並現在將Hybrid AF™治療列入Class 2建議。這些社會性指南反映了科學證據，顯示手術及混合消融對有房顫病患而言是安全且有效的。全球每年進行開胸手術的病患中，我們估計有超過500,000名病患為使用我們產品進行手術消融的潛在候選者，因為他們術前已有房顫。目前，我們估計這些候選者中不到15%接受手術消融治療。因此，我們認為我們的消融產品市場代表著一個重要的成長機會。

此外，Afib 被認為是美國每年約 800,000 起中風案例中約 15% 到 20% 的原因。根據美國心臟協會的資料，患有 Afib 的人中風風險高達五倍。研究也顯示，約 90% 的導致 Afib 病患中風的血塊來自左心耳（LAA）。2021 年，一項大型獨立國際隨機試驗《左心耳封閉試驗（LAAOS）III》顯示，在心臟手術中管理左心耳可顯著降低中風風險。Afib 每年在美國造成數十億美元的住院及門診費用。間接成本，如管理 Afib 相關中風，也被認為是相當高的。由於中風風險及對醫療體系的重大負擔，越來越多外科醫生在進行手術時會處理左心耳，這包括有 Afib 的病患以及沒有 Afib 但未來可能發病的病患。我們認為，我們的 AtriClip 系統比其他產品及技術更安全、更有效且更容易使用，用於心臟手術中排除左心耳。此外，我們的《預防性中風減少左心耳排除（LeAAPS）IDE 臨牀試驗》正在評估 AtriClip 系統在減少無預先 Afib 診斷的心臟手術病患中風的安全性與有效性。我們的《預防新發心房顫動的左心耳排除與_Box Lesion_ 手術（BoxX-NoAF）IDE 試驗》則評估同時使用 EnCompass 鋏與 AtriClip 系統進行消融對非 Afib 病患減少術後心房顫動（POAF）及臨牀 AF 的影響。因此，我們認為 AtriClip 系統的市場代表著一個重要的成長機會。

許多房顫（Afib）病患沒有其他潛在的心臟結構性疾病，尤其是那些有較進展性房顫形式的病患，會出現症狀，例如心悸、呼吸困難和嗜睡。這些病患通常有動機尋求治療以緩解其症狀。有症狀的病患通常由心律電生理學家使用導管消融術進行治療。導管消融術被認為是一種經皮的程序，不需要開胸；相反地，導管會透過陰囊的小穿刺插入。除了導管消融術，還有其他治療房顫病患的選擇，包括藥物治療（抗心律失常藥物）和植入式心律調節器。據估計，每年約有 500,000 名房顫病患在美國接受導管消融術治療，這個數字預期將持續顯著成長。雖然大多數接受導管消融術治療的陣發性房顫病患會經驗免除房顫，但少於三分之一的長期持續性房顫病患在接受導管消融術治療後一年內被治癒，且隨後這個比例會進一步下降。來自 CONVERGE™ IDE 臨牀試驗的隨機、前瞻性、多中心數據，以及多位醫師研究者進行的多項近期真實世界研究顯示，這些長期持續性房顫病患透過在心臟外表面進行消融，使用我們的 EPi-Sense® 消融系統，可以將成功比例提高超過一倍。因此，我們認為 EPi-Sense 消融系統用作最小侵入性或混合性 AF 治療，也代表本公司成長的機會。

除了房顫治療的機會，據估計，接受心臟手術且未被診斷為術前有房顫的病患中，有高達 50% 會最終發展為 POAF。有 POAF 的病患通常會有較差的急性及長期臨牀結果，包括發展為長期臨牀房顫的風險。此外，多項研究已將 POAF 與更高的醫療成本負擔相關聯。目前，尚無 FDA 批准的治療方式可預防心臟手術病患的 POAF 發生。十月，我們在 BoxX-NoAF IDE 試驗中納入了首位病患，該試驗旨在證明在心臟手術中進行消融及左心耳封閉術是安全且有效的，可減少 POAF 及長期臨牀房顫的風險，適用於那些術前無房顫病史的病患。如果試驗成功，我們認為這將大幅擴大我們對同時進行消融及左心耳封閉術的可接觸市場，使其包含無房顫病史的心臟手術病患。
涉及透過肋骨切口進行的胸腔手術，通常稱為胸腔切開術（thoracotomy access），以及心胸外科手術，常會導致術後顯著的疼痛和更長的住院復原時間，因為病患會避免在切口附近活動胸部。據估計，每年在美國約進行 150,0000 個胸腔手術及約 250,000 個心胸外科手術。住院復原時間會根據手術類型及手術相關的並發症而有所不同，範圍從兩到十五天不等

程序、疼痛管理協議及其他因素。大多數外科醫生會採用多模式疼痛管理協議，包含各種疼痛管理技術，包括 epidural 配藥直接在脊髓周圍、靜脈或口服給予阿片類與非阿片類止痛藥物，或其他策略。更聚焦的局部技術包括注射器注射於椎體之間與 Cryo Nerve Block，此技術使用冷凍能量來消融周圍神經，暫時停止來自胸壁的疼痛訊號傳導。神經「支架」保持完整，允許軸突再生並恢復神經功能。Cryo Nerve Block 可以透過我們的 cryoICE cryoSPHERE 探針來進行，這些探針是專門設計用於 Cryo Nerve Block 療法。根據手術的侵入性程度，醫生及其護理人員會利用多種方式來管理患者的疼痛。近年來，處方 narcotics，或阿片類藥物，因潛在的長期依賴性、過量服用及可能導致死亡而受到嚴格監督。美國聯邦與地方政府已提出並實施新的規範以遏制阿片類藥物過量的流行。估計有七分之一的胸腔手術患者會發展出對處方 narcotics 的不健康依賴，使替代性的非阿片類疼痛管理模式，如 Cryo Nerve Block，成為醫生管理術後疼痛的重要部分。我們認為我們的疼痛管理消融產品市場代表著重要的成長機會。2025 年 9 月，我們宣佈推出 cryoXT™ 裝置，這是一種創新冷凍消融技術，用來幫助管理截肢手術後的術後疼痛。每年，美國約有 180,000 例截肢手術，約有 60% 的患者會經歷殘肢疼痛，最高可達 85% 的患者報告有幻肢疼痛。隨著 cryoXT 裝置的推出，醫生現在可以使用新一代工具，將這種長期有效的術後截肢疼痛管理方法引入臨牀。Cryo Nerve Block 在心臟、胸腔及截肢手術以外的應用正在研究中，並代表未來可能的成長機會

我們認為目前我們在 Afib 與 LAAM 手術治療市場上為領導者，並為 Cryo Nerve Block 在心臟、胸腔及截肢手術中的應用先驅。我們預期在可預見的未來，我們的幾乎所有營業收入都與目前銷售或正在開發中的產品有關。我們的產品使外科醫生能夠以更快、更少侵入性且技術上較不困難的方式進行消融與 LAAM 手術，並有臨牀證實的結果。我們已完成，並持續投資於我們消融與 LAAM 產品在治療 Afib、減少術後 Afib 以及預防中風的臨牀研究。包括那些曾擔任或目前擔任我們顧問的領先外科醫生與電生理學家，已發表使用我們裝置的預臨牀與臨牀研究結果。這些研究結果已評估療效、易用性與安全性端點。
用於心臟組織消融的產品包括那些使用射頻（RF）能量或冷凍（cryo）模式來產生疤痕組織的產品。我們的消融產品是平台的一部分，每個平台包含可更換的手持裝置，連接到 RF 產生器或 cryo 產生器。我們通常將此類資本設備直接放置給我們的直接客戶，並銷售給我們的經銷商。

我們是治療心房顫動、左心耳管理及術後疼痛管理領域的領導創新者。我們的消融與左心耳管理產品由醫生在開胸手術與微創手術期間使用。在開胸手術中，醫生會為其他疾病進行心臟手術，而我們的產品會與（或"同時"進行）此種手術一起使用。微創手術則是獨立進行，通常會採用多學科或"混合"方式，結合使用AtriCure消融與LAAM產品的外科手術與電生理學家執行的導管消融手術。我們的疼痛管理設備由醫生用來消融周邊神經，提供心臟、胸腔與截肢手術的疼痛緩解。我們預期在可預見的未來，我們的收入幾乎全部與目前銷售或正在開發的產品相關。
我們透過美國、德國、法國、英國、比利時-荷蘭語區、澳洲與加拿大等地的直接銷售團隊，將產品銷售給醫療中心。我們也透過經銷商銷售產品，經銷商再將產品銷售至其他市場的醫療中心。我們的業務主要以美金進行交易；直接國際銷售則以歐元、英鎊、澳洲幣或加拿大幣進行交易。

2025年，我們實現了全球收入成長，這是因為我們的產品創新、臨牀科學與醫生教育與培訓策略，以擴大認知與採用。我們2025年12月31日財年的全球收入為534,528美元，較前一年成長14.9%，這是由於我們的疼痛管理、開胸消融與左心耳管理產品線的採用持續擴張所驅動。我們最近的產品發佈，包括cryoSPHERE MAX探針、AtriClip FLEX-Mini裝置與EnCompass夾具，對我們2025年的成長有顯著貢獻。我們的關鍵市場競爭對手有限；然而，新進企業正在開發與行銷競爭產品、程序與/或臨牀解決方案，這可能導致我們的結果出現變動。
2025年戰略與運營進展的重點包括：
左心耳管理。2025年第一季，FDA批准了AtriClip® PRO-Mini™ LAA Exclusion System的510(k) clearance。該裝置基於現有的AtriClip平台，預裝市場上最小的左心耳管理植入物。尺寸的減少為外科醫生在微創手術中提供更佳的視覺化，以精確且安全地排除左心耳。AtriClip PRO-Mini裝置於2025年下半年在美國上市。
疼痛管理。於 2025 年第二季，美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）授予 cryoICE® cryoXT™ 探針 510(k)  clearance，此為專門設計用於 Cryo Nerve Block 療法的 cryoablation 裝置，用以緩解截肢患者的疼痛。此裝置透過冷凍目標周邊神經，暫時停止疼痛，阻斷截肢部位的傳導路徑。於 2025 年第三季，此裝置於美國正式上市。

雙能量平台。於 2025 年第四季，我們成功執行了首例人體治療，使用我們新開發的雙能量平台，整合脈衝場消融（Pulsed Field Ablation, PFA）與先進射頻消融（Advanced Radiofrequency Ablation, Advanced RFA）技術。此新平台結合兩種技術的優點，將射頻（RF）消融已證實的安全性與 PFA 的效率相結合。先進 RFA 與 PFA 技術目前尚未在任何市場取得核准。我們預期在未來一年內啟動臨牀試驗，這將是我們產品開發流程中的重要里程碑。

effectiveness of radiofrequency (RF) ablation with the efficiency of PFA. The Advanced RFA and PFA technologies are not yet approved for use in any market. We expect to initiate a clinical trial in the coming year, marking a key milestone in our product development pipeline.
臨牀科學。我們投資於研究以擴展標籤聲請，支援我們產品的各種適應症，並發表涉及我們產品的治療與程序之臨牀數據。於 2025 年，我們支援了 13 篇文章及 15 場大會摘要的發表，內容為涉及我們產品之臨牀研究。

LeAAPS。左心耳封堵以預防中風之左心耳排除（LeAAPS）IDE 臨牀試驗，設計用以評估預防性左心耳排除使用 AtriClip 左心耳排除系統對心臟手術患者，其無預先 AF 診斷且有中風或系統性動脈栓塞風險之有效性。此前瞻性、多中心、隨機試驗評估 30 天術後之安全性，以顯示左心耳排除在心臟手術中不會增加風險，並評估至少術後五年追蹤期間之有效性。於 2025 年 7 月，我們完成全球 139 個中心共 6,573 名患者的試驗入組。患者追蹤持續進行中。

BoxX-NoAF。Box 損傷與左心耳排除程序以預防新發性心房顫動（BoxX-NoAF）IDE 試驗評估同時進行消融使用 EnCompass 夾具與左心耳排除使用 AtriClip 系統對非 AF 患者，以減少術後心房顫動（POAF）與臨牀心房顫動之影響。此前瞻性、多中心、多國隨機試驗評估 30 天術後之安全性以針對 POAF，並評估臨牀心房顫動之次要有效性至三年。試驗提供全球最多 75 個場地、最多 960 名受試者之入組。美國食品藥物管理局於 2024 年第四季批准試驗計畫，於 2025 年 10 月，我們完成首名受試者入組。場地啟動與入組持續進行中。

headings: 商業執行與產品表現風險
若本公司產品未能在美國取得廣泛市場接受度，將會對本公司營運成果造成損害，且本公司可能無法達成或維持獲利。
來自現有及新產品與程序的競爭可能會降低我們的市場佔有率，並可能導致我們的營業收入下降，並可能對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
有關我們產品所產生的臨牀數據可能不會正面，且我們目前及計畫中的臨牀試驗可能無法符合美國食品藥物管理局（FDA）或其他監管機構的要求。
總體經濟情況長時間惡化可能會對我們的業務產生重大且不利的影響。
過去十年醫療費用顯著上升。立法機構、監管機構及第三方付款機構可能已提出並可能持續提出控制或降低醫療費用的提案。
政府機構及第三方付款機構對手術程序的覆蓋範圍與報銷政策若出現不利變動，將會影響我們推廣與銷售產品的能力。
我們依賴單一及有限來源的第三方供應商與第三方服務提供者，這使我們容易受到供應問題與價格波動的影響，可能對我們的業務造成損害。
我們的製造業務高度集中，若我們製造設施出現中斷，可能會增加我們的費用並降低我們的營業收入。
若我們未能妥善管理預期的成長，將可能影響本公司業務。
關鍵資訊系統的中斷或系統安全的重大違規，可能對本公司業務、客戶關係及財務狀況造成損害。
我們的保險可能無法覆蓋因營運而產生的賠償義務及其他相關責任。
我們投入大量時間與金錢用以符合聯邦、州及外國法規，以及FDA法規，若未能完全遵守這些法規，將可能面臨重大處罰。
若未能遵守與本公司業務相關的廣泛FDA法規，可能遭受罰款、禁令及處罰，並可能影響本公司商業推廣及銷售產品的能力。
我們所銷售產品的使用可能導致傷害或其他不良事件，進而引發產品責任訴訟，這可能對本公司或客戶的業務造成高昂成本。
paragraphs: 以下對風險因素的討論包含向前看的陳述。這些風險因素可能對理解本報告中的其他陳述至關重要。以下資訊應與本報告中的其他資訊一併仔細考慮，包括管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析部分，以及合併財務報表及相關附註。若任何上述風險或不確定性實際發生或持續發生，可能對本公司業務、聲譽、財務狀況、營運成果、未來展望及股票價格造成重大且不利的影響。以下所列風險並非本公司所面臨的唯一風險，且可能出現目前未為本公司所知或目前認為不重要，但隨時間推移而變得重要或產生重大影響的風險，可能對本公司業務、聲譽、財務狀況、營運成果、未來展望或股票價格造成負面影響。這些因素出現的順序，不得解釋為表示其相對重要性或優先順序。
以下為可能對本公司業務、營運、財務結果及股票價格產生負面影響的主要風險摘要。
•未能在國內市場獲得廣泛接受，可能影響營運成果。
•來自現有及新產品與程序的競爭可能降低本公司市場佔有率。
•臨牀數據可能為負面，或本公司試驗可能無法符合監管當局的要求，可能延緩或反轉產品採用速度，或降低醫療界對本公司產品的使用率。
•對某些國際市場銷售產品依賴獨立經銷商，可能對本公司銷售造成不利影響。
